diagram_math_checks.objects: Near-case open balls B_i, B_{i+1}, B_{i+2} in a plane through the centre line, for i>=1 and d>0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.2 defines x_j=x+2^{-j}(x_0-x) and r_j=2^{-j-1}d. Coordinates along that line, translated/rotated/rescaled, give x=(0,0), x_i=(4,0), x_{i+1}=(2,0), x_{i+2}=(1,0), radii 2,1,1/2. Thus |x_j-x|=2r_j, r_{j+1}=r_j/2 and |x_j-x_{j+1}|=r_j, exactly as drawn. This is not a depiction of general far-case monotone radii.

In normalized coordinates z=(2.5,0) and radius=0.5. Distances to x_i and x_{i+1} are 1.5=3r_i/4 and 0.5=r_i/4. For every point in the open witness ball, triangle inequalities give distance strictly less than 2 to x_i and strictly less than 1 to x_{i+1}; therefore it lies in B_i intersection B_{i+1}, the overlap construction of step 1.2.

All four drawn circles are boundary outlines of open balls, not closed-disk assertions. Four solid dots mark actual points x and the three centres. The dotted segment and ellipsis point toward the omitted later centres approaching x by step 1.2. The bidirectional dimension arrow asserts only the centre separation r_i. No domain boundary, additional domain geometry, morphism, commutativity or graph cycle is asserted. Figure is outside Facts/Proof, whose bytes are unchanged.
